reference_sql:
SELECT c.parent_category,
       COUNT(*) AS n_new_products,
       ROUND(AVG(f.first_sale_date - f.launch_date), 1) AS avg_days_to_first_sale
FROM (
  -- one row per product launched in 2024 or 2025 that sold at least once
  SELECT p.product_id, p.category_id, p.launch_date, MIN(s.order_date) AS first_sale_date
  FROM products AS p
  JOIN sales AS s ON s.product_id = p.product_id
  WHERE p.launch_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31'
  GROUP BY p.product_id, p.category_id, p.launch_date
) AS f
JOIN categories AS c ON c.category_id = f.category_id
GROUP BY c.parent_category
ORDER BY c.parent_category
alternatives:
WITH first_sales AS (
  -- one row per product launched in 2024 or 2025 that sold at least once
  SELECT p.product_id, p.category_id, p.launch_date, MIN(s.order_date) AS first_sale_date
  FROM products AS p
  JOIN sales AS s ON s.product_id = p.product_id
  WHERE p.launch_date >= DATE '2024-01-01'
    AND p.launch_date <= DATE '2025-12-31'
  GROUP BY p.product_id, p.category_id, p.launch_date
)
SELECT c.parent_category,
       COUNT(*) AS n_new_products,
       ROUND(AVG(date_diff('day', f.launch_date, f.first_sale_date)), 1) AS avg_days_to_first_sale
FROM first_sales AS f
JOIN categories AS c ON c.category_id = f.category_id
GROUP BY c.parent_category
ORDER BY c.parent_category

SELECT c.parent_category,
       COUNT(*) AS n_new_products,
       ROUND(AVG((SELECT MIN(s.order_date) FROM sales AS s WHERE s.product_id = p.product_id) - p.launch_date), 1) AS avg_days_to_first_sale
FROM products AS p
JOIN categories AS c ON c.category_id = p.category_id
WHERE p.launch_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31'
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sales AS s2 WHERE s2.product_id = p.product_id)
GROUP BY c.parent_category
ORDER BY c.parent_category

SELECT f.parent_category,
       COUNT(*) AS n_new_products,
       ROUND(AVG(date_diff('day', f.launch_date, f.first_sale_date)), 1) AS avg_days_to_first_sale
FROM (
  -- one row per product launched in 2024 or 2025 that sold at least once
  SELECT p.product_id, c.parent_category, p.launch_date, MIN(CAST(o.order_ts AS DATE)) AS first_sale_date
  FROM products AS p
  JOIN categories AS c ON c.category_id = p.category_id
  JOIN order_lines AS ol ON ol.product_id = p.product_id
  JOIN orders AS o ON o.order_id = ol.order_id
  WHERE p.launch_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31'
  GROUP BY p.product_id, c.parent_category, p.launch_date
) AS f
GROUP BY f.parent_category
ORDER BY f.parent_category

WITH first_sales AS (

  SELECT p.product_id, p.category_id, p.launch_date, MIN(s.order_date) AS first_sale_date
  FROM products AS p
  JOIN sales AS s ON s.product_id = p.product_id
  WHERE p.launch_date >= DATE '2024-01-01'
    AND p.launch_date <= DATE '2025-12-31'
  GROUP BY p.product_id, p.category_id, p.launch_date
)
SELECT c.parent_category,
       COUNT(*) AS n_new_products,
       ROUND(AVG(date_diff('day', f.launch_date, f.first_sale_date)), 1) AS avg_days_to_first_sale
FROM first_sales AS f
JOIN categories AS c ON c.category_id = f.category_id
GROUP BY c.parent_category
ORDER BY c.parent_category
other_way.tradeoff: A WITH step with date_diff reads top to bottom, and for whole days date_diff gives the same count as subtracting the dates.

solver.query:
WITH f AS (
  SELECT ol.product_id, MIN(CAST(CAST(o.order_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS DATE)) AS first_sale
  FROM order_lines ol
  JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = ol.order_id
  GROUP BY ol.product_id
)
SELECT c.parent_category,
       COUNT(*) AS n_new_products,
       ROUND(AVG(date_diff('day', CAST(p.launch_date AS DATE), f.first_sale)), 1) AS avg_days_to_first_sale
FROM products p
JOIN f ON f.product_id = p.product_id
JOIN categories c ON c.category_id = p.category_id
WHERE CAST(p.launch_date AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2024-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31'
GROUP BY c.parent_category
ORDER BY c.parent_category
